Article Title: India, Italy target €20bn trade by 2029, explore economic corridor linking Asia and Europe
Article Text:

India and Italy have set a target of raising bilateral trade to €20 billion by 2029, from €14.2 billion in 2025. The two countries also plan to set up task forces to ease business operations and explore an economic corridor linking Asia and Europe.The decisions were discussed during a meeting between Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal and Italian deputy prime minister and foreign minister Antonio Tajani in Rome on November 18, according to Italy's ministry of foreign affairs.The two sides also discussed the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), which aims to connect Indian markets with Europe through the Middle East using rail and maritime networks.Italy is looking to strengthen the role of its Mediterranean ports in the proposed corridor. Tajani identified the port of Trieste as a potential gateway for goods moving towards Central and Eastern Europe.Separately, the two countries have agreed to establish task forces in India and Italy to help businesses overcome bureaucratic and administrative hurdles. According to the Italian foreign ministry, the task forces will work to simplify procedures and facilitate trade and investment between the two countries.The Italian foreign ministry said IMEC could create new opportunities in trade, logistics and energy connectivity. For India, the proposed route could offer an additional link to European markets and help diversify supply chains.India and Italy are also exploring the establishment of an Innovation Hub in India, modelled on Italy's INNOVIT Centre in San Francisco. The proposed hub would bring together startups, businesses and research institutions to promote technology partnerships, innovation and investment.The two countries also discussed expanding cooperation in pharmaceuticals, chemicals, industrial machinery, automobiles, aerospace, agriculture and renewable energy. According to India's Press Information Bureau (PIB), sectoral discussions focused on technology transfer, joint research, electric mobility, food processing and advanced manufacturing.The meeting also covered the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA). According to the PIB, both sides welcomed the conclusion of negotiations and discussed how the pact could improve market access, boost investments and strengthen supply chains. Italy stressed the need for its early signing.
Article Summary: India and Italy have set a target of raising bilateral trade to €20 billion by 2029, from €14.2 billion in 2025. The two countries also plan to set up task forces to ease business operations and explore an economic corridor linking Asia and Europe.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle-age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests.Under the new rules, notified on November 13, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity, while older vehicles will have to undergo emission tests at shorter intervals. The revised framework also standardises PUC certificate validity for older emission categories across the country, replacing variations in testing requirements between states.The changes have been introduced through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amend Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The amendment came into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.Previously, the validity of a PUC certificate was determined primarily by the vehicle's Bharat Stage (BS) emission category. Consequently, a newly registered private car and an older commercial vehicle, despite belonging to the BS-VI category, were both eligible for a certificate valid for one year.The revised framework introduces a more differentiated approach for BS-VI vehicles. Certificate validity will now depend on two factors:The vehicle's age will be calculated from the date of its first registration.Under the earlier system, all private BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for 12 months, irrespective of their age.The revised rules introduce three validity brackets:This means owners of newer private BS-VI vehicles will have to undergo emission testing less frequently, while those with vehicles older than 10 years will face more frequent testing.Commercial BS-VI vehicles will also be subject to an age-based validity schedule, although the extension for newer vehicles will be shorter than that available to private vehicles.Previously, all commercial BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for one year. Under the amended rules:The revised schedule therefore offers longer validity to newer commercial vehicles, but retains more frequent testing requirements for older ones.The amendment also introduces a uniform testing requirement for vehicles conforming to older emission standards.Previously, BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles were generally subject to a six-month PUC certificate validity under the central rules. However, some states had prescribed shorter intervals. Delhi, for instance, already required these vehicles to undergo emission testing every three months.Under the revised framework, the validity period for all BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will be three months, irrespective of their age or category.This makes the three-month testing requirement applicable uniformly across all states and Union territories.For BS-IV vehicles, the earlier central provision allowed a PUC certificate validity of 12 months. However, certain states and areas within the national capital region (NCR) had already imposed a shorter six-month validity.The amended rules now prescribe six months as the standard validity period for all BS-IV vehicles across the country, irrespective of whether they are private or commercial.The change effectively brings the national requirement in line with the stricter timelines already followed in some regions.The amendment also clarifies how the validity period of a renewed PUC certificate will be calculated, depending on when the vehicle owner undergoes the emission test.Renewal within 10 days before expiry: If the vehicle undergoes testing within the 10 days preceding the expiry of its existing certificate, the renewed certificate will take effect from the expiry date of the previous certificate. This ensures that owners do not lose any remaining validity by renewing early.Renewal on or after expiry: If the test is conducted on or after the existing certificate's expiry date, the renewed certificate will be valid from the date of the test.PUC certificates issued before the amended rules came into force will remain valid until their respective expiry dates.Vehicle owners do not need to obtain fresh certificates immediately to comply with the revised schedule. The new validity provisions will apply when they renew their existing certificates for the first time under the amended rules.For instance, a private BS-VI car that is four years old and currently holds a one-year PUC certificate will become eligible for a three-year certificate at its next renewal. The revised validity will not automatically extend the certificate it already holds.All vehicles must have a valid PUC certificate issued by a testing centre authorised by the respective state government.Under Rule 116 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, vehicle owners are required to produce the certificate when demanded by an authorised official. Its validity can also be verified digitally through the Parivahan PUCC Portal.Under the earlier provisions, new vehicles across emission categories were exempt from obtaining a separate PUC certificate for the first year following their initial registration. However, the available details of the latest amendment do not clarify whether this exemption has been altered or retained.
Article Summary: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle- age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests. Under the new rules, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity. Older vehicles will have to undergo tests at shorter intervals.

Article Title: Delhi HC clarifies restaurants have no interim relief to levy mandatory service charges
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Thursday clarified that it has not granted any interim relief to restaurants allowing them to continue charging mandatory service charges from customers, despite an earlier judgment declaring the practice illegal.A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma said no interim protection had been granted to restaurant associations against the March 28, 2025, judgment of a single judge, which upheld the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) guidelines prohibiting compulsory service charges.The clarification came after Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the government told the court that some restaurants were still making service charges mandatory for customers, contrary to the High Court's earlier ruling, ANI reported.Sharma submitted that restaurants could not continue the practice after the single judge had upheld the CCPA guidelines prohibiting hotels and restaurants from automatically adding service charges to food bills.Responding to the submission, the bench said it had not granted any interim relief to the restaurant associations in their appeals."Where is the interim relief? Where is the interim relief in their favour? We have not granted any interim prayer," Acting Chief Justice Sambre remarked.The court was hearing appeals filed by the National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) and the Federation of Hotel and Restaurant Associations of India (FHRAI) against the single judge's March 2025 judgment.On March 28, 2025, Justice Prathiba M Singh dismissed petitions filed by NRAI and FHRAI challenging the CCPA guidelines issued on July 4, 2022.The single judge ruled that restaurants cannot make service charges compulsory, even if they are mentioned on menus. Customers cannot be forced to pay such charges, which must remain voluntary.The court held that collecting service charges without a customer's consent amounts to an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. It also upheld the CCPA's authority to issue guidelines to protect consumer rights and prevent unfair trade practices, imposing costs of Rs 1 lakh on the restaurant associations.The judgment further said restaurants cannot automatically add service charges to bills. Customers must be informed that any additional payment towards service or staff welfare is voluntary.The single judge had also expressed concern over the use of the term 'service charge', observing that it could mislead customers into believing it was a government-imposed tax.In their appeals, NRAI and FHRAI argued that collecting service charges was a practice followed by the hospitality industry for more than 80 years and should not be treated as an unfair trade practice.NRAI contended that restaurants which clearly disclose service charges on their menus and inform customers before they place orders should be allowed to collect them.The association argued that service charges are not merely additional earnings for restaurants but are distributed among employees, including waiters, kitchen staff and other workers. It said the system also ensures that employees who do not directly interact with customers receive a share of the collection.The restaurant associations questioned whether the issue should be governed by consumer protection laws or labour laws, particularly when charges are clearly disclosed to customers.They also referred to judicial decisions, labour settlements and wage-related arrangements recognising service charges, including the Supreme Court's 1964 judgment in Management of Wenger & Co. v. Their Workmen.The CCPA issued guidelines on July 4, 2022, prohibiting hotels and restaurants from automatically adding service charges to food bills.The move followed consumer complaints that establishments were adding charges, generally ranging from 5% to 20%, without seeking customers' consent.NRAI approached the Delhi HC on July 18, 2022, challenging the guidelines. FHRAI later filed a separate petition raising similar objections.On July 20, 2022, the High Court stayed the operation of the CCPA guidelines while issuing notices on the petitions.The restaurant associations argued that the guidelines were arbitrary and would adversely affect the hospitality industry. They maintained that service charges were an established practice and helped ensure fair distribution of earnings among restaurant employees.They also pointed out that similar charges were collected in several countries, including the United Kingdom, Singapore, Japan and the United States.However, in March 2025, the single judge rejected their arguments and upheld the CCPA guidelines, ruling that restaurants cannot force customers to pay service charges. The associations have now challenged that decision before the Division Bench.
Article Summary: Delhi high court says it has not granted any interim relief to restaurants allowing them to continue charging mandatory service charges from customers. The clarification came after Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma told the court that some restaurants were still making service charges mandatory for customers. Sharma submitted that restaurants could not continue the practice after the single judge had upheld the CCPA guidelines.

NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant's decision to withdraw two cases from the bench headed by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah, which had expanded individual incidents of lapses on the part of authorities into pan-India judicial drives against similar illegalities, averted a potential religious controversy.The bench's Aug 4 order directing all states and UTs to remove stray animals from public places created a controversy as it is known that the majority of strays comprise cows and calves. A UP resident filed an application before the bench apprehending that the order was "capable of being implemented in a manner that may result in cows and their progeny being rounded up, transported or disposed of without regard to the special constitutional protection they are entitled to".Also Read| SC starts contempt case against lawyer for remarks against CJI The applicant said, "Cows have been worshipped and revered in Indian society since ancient times as 'gaumata', and religious sentiments of the public..., particularly the Hindu community, are gravely hurt whenever cows are slaughtered or otherwise ill-treated."He said a blanket order for the removal of strays by SC ran "the real risk of stray cattle being pushed across state borders, herded into inadequate holding pounds, or otherwise subjected to conditions violative of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960...instead of being rehabilitated through properly funded and regulated gaushalas".The CJI's decision to withdraw the cases, backed by the four most senior SC judges, was taken after they felt it was impermissible for a bench, not assigned the PIL roster, to create PIL jurisdiction for itself by expanding individual cases into pan-India exercises in violation of case-distribution discipline, which falls in the CJI's domain.SC sources said the CJI informed the senior judges there would be a general survey of cases before other benches to identify matters where the ambit had been expanded to give these a pan-India texture by converting them into PILs. A decision on allocation to appropriate benches would be taken after that, they said.One such case - Loganathan vs State of Tamil Nadu - started from the illegal construction of a ground plus one floor without a sanction plan and the failure of authorities to even notice it. The bench led by Justice Amanullah on March 25 said, "It is evident there are apparent widespread and blatant violations of building bylaws and land-use regulations. In view of the above, we deem it appropriate to examine the issue on a pan-India basis. " It impleaded municipal corporations and municipalities of capital cities of all states and UTs.

NEW DELHI: Azam Khan , former Samajwadi Party MP from Rampur and one of the most powerful cabinet ministers during the SP govt's term in UP in 2012-17, allegedly used the entire state machinery to build a private university over hundreds of acres of "illegally" occupied land, including agricultural fields and around 34 acres of enemy property.DThe ED last month attached land and buildings of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the trust running it, and estimated its market value at over Rs 1,170 crore. According to the agency's investigation and FIRs, Khan had forcefully "occupied" agricultural land from farmers in Singankhera village in Rampur to build the private university, of which he is the chancellor."Farmers were coerced through assault, unlawful confinement and threats into executing sale deeds in its favour," the ED claimed. When he was urban development minister in UP, "funds and material meant for public works were diverted to the university, govt works were executed on its private campus, and funds from contractors who had been allotted govt contracts were routed back to the trust as donations", the agency claimed.Khan held several important portfolios, including urban development, water supplies, waqf and minority welfare during 2012-17.In this period, he awarded several govt contracts to his Rampur constituency but also oversaw "demolition" of houses of tenants of waqf property. Ironically, he was then the minister for waqf and minority welfare. Funds came from several sources as 'donations' - Rs 6 crore from two Meerut-based educational entities through "political influence", Rs 23 crore from the UP govt for construction of an OBC boys' hostel and a hospital block in the university campus.Khan has over 25 FIRs filed against him in Rampur, and multiple money laundering investigations by ED. "In 2016, houses of several families in Rampur city, many of them tenants of waqf property, were demolished with bulldozers by a mob allegedly led by the then circle officer and others on the instructions of Azam Khan. The occupants were assaulted, threatened with false criminal cases, and robbed of their cash, jewellery and cattle," the ED said in one of its reports. Khan also ensured that debris of the demolished houses were used for laying the foundation of Jauhar University, the ED claimed.
Article Summary: Azam Khan was one of the most powerful cabinet ministers during the SP govt's term in UP in 2012-17. He allegedly used the entire state machinery to build a private university over hundreds of acres of "illegally" occupied land. The ED last month attached land and buildings of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.

Article Title: Major KFC franchisee files for bankruptcy protection, may shut more outlets
Article Text:
A KFC logo is displayed above a restaurant

A major KFC franchisee in the US has filed for bankruptcy protection, citing rising costs and declining sales, after shutting dozens of restaurants this year. The company has warned that more outlets could close as it seeks to restructure its operations and exit additional leases.Tasty Chick’n LLC, which operates 75 KFC outlets and nine restaurants co-branded with Taco Bell across 10 US states, including Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, filed for bankruptcy on Monday. Court documents show that it owes about $16 million in unpaid royalties to Yum Brands Inc, KFC’s parent company.The franchisee said it sought Chapter 11 protection to prevent Yum from immediately terminating its franchise agreement. It has shut 44 locations since the beginning of 2026 and plans to use the bankruptcy process to exit more leases, according to court filings, Bloomberg reported.Chapter 11 is a form of bankruptcy in the United States that allows a struggling business, or, less commonly, an individual, to reorganise its debts and operations while continuing to stay open and operateIn a Tuesday filing, a Yum affiliate said it had been working with Tasty Chick’n for several months.However, it alleged that the franchisee’s sudden restaurant closures had significantly damaged the KFC brand, leaving it absent from some markets and weakening its presence and consumer confidence in those communities.Tasty Chick’n is at least the third major restaurant franchisee to seek bankruptcy protection in recent weeks. An operator of Outback Steakhouse restaurants filed for Chapter 11 earlier this month, also citing rising costs.In September, a major Wendy’s franchisee sought court protection while owing more than $147 million in royalties and fees to the burger chain’s corporate owner.The KFC franchisee employs more than 1,600 people, most of them full-time workers, according to court papers. It has filed customary motions seeking permission to continue paying wages and meeting other operating expenses while it operates under Chapter 11.
Article Summary: Tasty Chick’n LLC operates 75 KFC outlets and nine restaurants co-branded with Taco Bell across 10 US states. The company has warned that more outlets could close as it seeks to restructure its operations and exit additional leases.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), one of the most anticipated video games in recent years, to showcase India's economic and infrastructure transformation, drawing a comparison between the country's progress during the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA 6."India is playing a whole new game!" Modi said in a post on X, sharing a series of colourful graphics styled around the popular Grand Theft Auto video game franchise.Titled 'Between GTA V and VI, here's how India upgraded', the graphics compare India's position in several sectors during the period between the release of GTA V in 2013 and GTA VI in 2026. The comparison covers economic growth, poverty reduction, sanitation, renewable energy and the space sector.The post uses the gaming franchise's long-awaited return as a reference point to present India's development over the past 13 years.One of the graphics compares India's economic position, describing the country as part of the 'Fragile Five' economies during the GTA V era and portraying it as the world's fastest-growing major economy in the GTA VI era.The comparison reflects India's changing economic position over the past decade, with the country emerging as a major growth centre in the global economy.Another graphic focuses on poverty reduction, showing extreme poverty declining from 27% in the 'Then' category to 2.6% in the 'Now' category.The illustration contrasts a cluster of thatched houses with a modern home and a family, presenting the change as an indicator of improvements in living conditions.The graphics also highlight India's sanitation drive, showing sanitation mission completion rising from 39% to 100%.The comparison features children using dustbins and a public sanitation facility, alongside the Swachh Bharat Mission logo.The renewable energy sector is another focus of the post. The graphic shows India's solar capacity increasing from 2.82 GW to 175 GW.It contrasts workers installing solar panels with a large solar power installation, presenting the expansion of renewable energy infrastructure as another marker of India's transformation.The final comparison focuses on India's space sector and the growth of private participation in space technology.The graphic shows the number of space startups increasing from one during the earlier period to 440 in the present, depicting workers assembling a rocket in a modern manufacturing facility.The comparison reflects the expansion of India's private space ecosystem following the opening up of the sector to private players.Meanwhile, Congress on took a swipe at PM Modi after he invoked the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, or GTA 6, saying it was very appropriate as the video game follows a “criminal duo”.Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said, “The PM, in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth, has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media.”“Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate,” he said on X.An action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI was rolled out across the globe on Thursday, marking its entry into the GTA series following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V.PM Modi's post coincides with the global release of Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V was released in September 2013.Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA VI returns players to Vice City, a fictionalised version of Miami, and follows the story of protagonists Jason and Lucia. The game is launching on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.The long gap between the two instalments has made GTA VI one of the most anticipated entertainment releases, with Rockstar building expectations through trailers, promotional campaigns and pre-release announcements.By using the franchise's return as a timeline, Modi's post draws a parallel between the evolution of the gaming series and India's development across economic, infrastructure and technology sectors over the same period.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) to showcase India's economic and infrastructure transformation. He drew a comparison between the country's progress during the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA 6. The post uses the gaming franchise's long-awaited return as a reference point to present India's development.

Article Title: Govt hospitals to hike Ayushman packages from 23 to 112
Article Text:
The focus is on treatments that can be provided at govt facilities, particularly community health centres and sub-divisional hospitals (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: Patients covered under Ayushman Bharat may soon get access to a wider range of routine medical treatments and surgical procedures, with govt proposing to expand packages reserved for public health facilities under the scheme from 23 to 112.The 89 additional packages cover conditions such as anaemia, hypertension, bronchitis, diarrhoea, urinary tract infections and diabetes-related complications. Procedures include hysterectomy, circumcision, biopsy and treatment for haemorrhoids, cysts and lipomas, besides screening for diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma.The focus is on treatments that can be provided at govt facilities, particularly community health centres and sub-divisional hospitals, subject to infrastructure and staff availability.Since 2019, 23 packages covering obstetrics, gynaecology and mental health have been reserved for public facilities. National Health Authority has invited states to suggest changes by Nov 25. The revised framework is proposed to take effect from Dec 1, after considering their feedback.
Article Summary: Patients covered under Ayushman Bharat may soon get access to a wider range of routine medical treatments and surgical procedures. Govt proposing to expand packages reserved for public health facilities under the scheme from 23 to 112. 89 additional packages cover conditions such as anaemia, hypertension, bronchitis, diarrhoea, urinary tract infections and diabetes-related complications.

NEW DELHI: Ahead of India-Japan 2+2 dialogue, external affairs minister S Jaishankar has underlined the significance of defence and security cooperation between the two countries as well as greater scope for collaboration in areas like advanced manufacturing, critical minerals and semiconductors.Jaishankar and defence minister Rajnath Singh are in Japan for the 4th 2+2 dialogue. He also called for deeper cooperation in clean energy and pharmaceuticals.He listed shocks to the international system, weaponisation and chokepoints, extreme competition and greater risk-taking, de-risking and diversification, and trusted partnerships as five defining features of the current state of the world."As two leading nations of the region committed to maintaining a free and open Indo-Pacific, India and Japan obviously have to secure their own national interests in this regard. India's Hindu population is projected to increase by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, but Hindus are expected to account for a slightly smaller share of the country's population as Muslims continue to have higher fertility rates, according to new projections by the Pew Research Center.Despite the projected shift, Hindus are expected to continue making up more than three-quarters of India's population by 2070.The global Hindu population is also projected to grow by 199 million over the same period, reaching nearly 1.4 billion. However, as the rest of the world's population is expected to grow at a faster pace, Hindus' share of the global population is projected to decline from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070.The projections are part of a broader Pew Research Center study examining changes in the size and composition of major religious groups between 2020 and 2070. The estimates take into account differences in fertility rates, age profiles, religious switching and international migration.Pew said that although India's overall fertility rate has declined rapidly in recent decades, Muslim women continue to have more children on average than Hindu women.Combined with the younger age profile of India's Muslim population, this fertility gap is expected to increase the Muslim share of the country's population while reducing the Hindu share.India had 1.1 billion Hindus in 2020, accounting for around 95% of the global Hindu population. Nepal, with 24 million Hindus, Bangladesh with 13 million, Pakistan with 5 million and Indonesia with 4 million made up the other countries in the top five.The rankings are expected to change by 2070, with the United States projected to have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Australia is also expected to enter the top 10, ranking ninth with around 3 million Hindus, while the United Arab Emirates is projected to drop out of the list.Pakistan's Hindu population is expected to double to 10 million by 2070, although the country is projected to retain its fourth position in the global rankings.Outside India, much of the projected growth in the Hindu population is expected to come from Pakistan and the United States. Pakistan is likely to see an increase primarily through natural population growth, with births outnumbering deaths, while immigration is expected to be the main driver of growth in the US.The Asia-Pacific region, home to 99% of the world's Hindus, is projected to account for most of the community's growth over the next five decades. Its Hindu population is expected to increase by 191 million between 2020 and 2070.Hindus are projected to make up 28% of the region's population by 2070, compared with 26% in 2020.In North America, the Hindu population is expected to more than double from 4 million in 2020 to 9 million in 2070. Their share of the region's population is projected to increase from 1% to 2%.Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean are the only regions where the Hindu population is projected to decline in absolute numbers. If current trends continue, Hindus will account for less than 0.1% of the population in each of these regions by 2070.Pew's projections identify fertility, mortality, age structure, international migration and religious switching as the key factors determining changes in the size of religious groups.The global Hindu population is expected to gain more than 200 million people through natural increase between 2020 and 2070, with nearly all of this growth projected to take place in the Asia-Pacific region.Religious switching is expected to have little impact on the overall Hindu population. Pew said this is partly because Hindus have a high retention rate, with an estimated 99% of people raised Hindu continuing to identify with the religion as adults.The corresponding retention rates are 85% among Christians and 83% among Buddhists. Muslims have a retention rate of 99%, on a par with Hindus.Overall, religious switching is projected to reduce the global Hindu population by around 1 million people between 2020 and 2070, with most of the losses expected in the Asia-Pacific region.Migration, meanwhile, is expected to contribute significantly to Hindu population growth in North America, the Middle East-North Africa region and Europe. Together, these regions are projected to gain more than 8 million Hindus through migration by 2070.Asia and the Pacific is expected to record the largest migration-related losses. However, the region's gains through natural population growth are projected to far exceed the number of Hindus it loses through emigration.The Pew report also projects that Islam will overtake Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, as the Muslim population continues to grow at a faster pace.Both religions are expanding globally, but Pew attributed the faster growth of Islam largely to higher fertility rates among Muslims.“It's the babies,” said Conrad Hackett, a senior demographer at Pew, explaining that fertility rates play a much greater role in religious population growth than conversion and other forms of religious switching.During 2020-2025, the fertility rate among Muslim women stood at 3.1 children per woman, compared with 2.5 among Christian women. The average for women belonging to all other religious groups was 1.6, below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman needed for each generation to replace itself.According to Pew's latest estimates, there were 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims worldwide in 2020. The new projections indicate that the Muslim population will reach 2.57 billion by 2035, overtaking the Christian population, which is expected to stand at 2.52 billion.If current trends continue, the number of Muslims worldwide will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the Christian population is projected to remain just below 3 billion.The projections also point to significant changes in the religious composition of North America.The United States, where Christians currently account for 62% of the population, is projected to lose its Christian majority by 2065. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to make up 41% of the US population.In neighbouring Canada, Christians are projected to account for less than half of the population by 2030. By 2070, people with no religious affiliation are expected to outnumber Christians in the country.The rise in the number of people identifying with no religion is a significant factor behind the projected decline in the Christian share of the population in both countries.

Article Title: Child's spectacle power rising? Myopia may be more than just weak eyesight
Article Text:
The rise in spectacle power among children could signal a risk for myopia, which might result in future eye problems.

NEW DELHI:

If your child's spectacle power keeps increasing, it may be more than just a change in eyesight. Childhood myopia, or short-sightedness, can involve the gradual elongation of the eyeball, increasing the risk of certain eye complications later in life, doctors warn.One common misconception among parents is that wearing spectacles makes eyesight weaker. Doctors say correctly prescribed glasses do not worsen myopia. However, ordinary spectacles correct blurred vision but do not necessarily slow its progression.Myopia allows children to see nearby objects clearly but makes distant objects appear blurred. Its development is linked to several factors, including family history, prolonged near-work activities and limited outdoor time. Mobile phones alone are not responsible, and even children who rarely use digital devices can develop the condition."An increase in the length of the eyeball, known as axial elongation, is an important aspect of myopia. Higher degrees of myopia are associated with a greater risk of certain eye problems later in life," said Dr Digvijay Singh, director, Noble Eye Care and paediatric ophthalmologist.Spending around two hours outdoors daily can help reduce the risk of developing myopia, although its ability to slow progression in children who already have the condition is less certain.Eye exercises, meanwhile, cannot reverse structural myopia or shorten an elongated eyeball. Taking breaks during reading and screen use can ease eye strain but does not treat myopia.Several options are now available to slow its progression in suitable children, including low-dose atropine eye drops, specially designed spectacle lenses and specialised contact lenses. Treatment must be tailored by an eye specialist, as results vary.Doctors also stress that children may not recognise changes in their eyesight, making regular eye examinations important even when they appear to see clearly. Follow-ups help monitor spectacle power, eye growth and response to treatment.During National Myopia Week (November 14-20), under the #ActOnMyopia campaign, specialists are urging parents to seek timely eye examinations and not dismiss increasing spectacle power as a routine childhood issue.
Article Summary: Myopia allows children to see nearby objects clearly but makes distant objects appear blurred. Development linked to several factors, including family history, prolonged near-work activities and limited outdoor time. Mobile phones alone are not responsible, and even children who rarely use digital devices can develop the condition.

NEW DELHI: India launched a sharp attack on Pakistan at a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) meeting, accusing its military establishment of exploiting the country's natural resources for personal gain and fomenting conflict with neighbouring countries at the expense of its own people.Speaking at an Arria-formula meeting convened by Liberia on natural resources and conflict, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, hit back after the Pakistani delegation raised the Indus Waters Treaty Harish said New Delhi had no intention of bringing bilateral issues into the discussion but was compelled to respond to Pakistan's attempt to misuse the forum."Mr. Chair, it was not our intention to bring other issues into this forum, but my delegation is compelled to respond to the comment made by the delegation of Pakistan that has chosen to misuse today's discussion to peddle its propaganda. Our position on the Indus Waters Treaty remains clear and consistent and has been articulated at multiple fora," he said.Targeting Pakistan's military establishment, Harish referred to an incident involving army chief Asim Munir, who was seen displaying a wooden case containing mineral stones to foreign leaders. He pointed out that the military's involvement in resource exploitation was also linked to political developments within Pakistan, including the removal of an elected provincial government and the imposition of a state of emergency.He said, "Their army chief was seen last September displaying a wooden box filled with mineral stones to foreign leaders, a clear indication of their army's role in this exploitation, which is also believed to be behind the recent dismissal of a provincial government in Pakistan and imposition of a state of emergency there."Last year, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir were photographed presenting rare earth minerals to US President Donald Trump at the White House. The photograph showed Munir gesturing towards an open wooden case containing the minerals, while Trump looked inside and Sharif stood nearby.The Indian envoy further lashed out Pakistan's military leadership of prioritising its own interests over the welfare of ordinary citizens and warned that its policy of fomenting conflict with neighbouring countries was hurting Pakistan itself."Pakistanis would be served well if its real rulers, its military, used the country's natural resources for the benefit of their population rather than self-aggrandisement. They would also be served better if the Pakistani army stops fomenting conflict for its neighbours, which is actually boomerang-ing back to bite their own country," the envoy said.Beyond the exchange with Pakistan, Harish outlined India's position on the responsible management of natural resources, arguing that illegal mining and smuggling can finance armed groups and prolong conflicts instead of contributing to national development.Thanking Liberia for convening the discussion, he said, "Liberia's own journey from conflict to recovery lends particular weight to this exchange."Harish called for greater reliance on existing voluntary international mechanisms rather than creating new frameworks to regulate natural resource trade. He cited the Kimberley Process, an international certification scheme aimed at preventing the trade in conflict diamonds, as an example of effective cooperation between governments, industry and civil society."Our experience is that cooperation works best when it is voluntary, consensus-based, and nationally led in an environment of friendship and goodwill. The Kimberley Process is an instructive example. By bringing together governments, industry, and civil society, it has curbed the trade in conflict diamonds while keeping legitimate trade open. As chair of the Kimberley Process in 2026, India is committed to strengthening its effectiveness and inclusiveness. Existing and tested mechanisms deserve to be fully utilised, and wherever feasible replicated, before new frameworks are contemplated," he said.Emphasising the need to ensure that local communities benefit from resources extracted from their land, Harish pointed to India's mining laws, under which companies are required to contribute towards the development of mining-affected areas.He also stressed the need to respect the distinct mandates of various UN bodies, arguing that the Security Council should focus on international peace and security, while broader issues of sustainable development and resource governance should be addressed by other institutions."As these discussions evolve, we should preserve the distinct mandates of the principal organs of the United Nations. The Security Council's responsibility is the maintenance of international peace and security. Broader questions of sustainable development and resource governance belong to the General Assembly, the ECOSOC, and other relevant bodies. The Peacebuilding Commission, given its inclusive composition, can support nationally owned efforts in this area. India stands ready to share its experience and to work with all partners towards practical, consensus-based approaches that enable natural resources to drive sustainable development and lasting peace," he said.
Article Summary: India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, hit back after the Pakistani delegation raised the Indus Waters Treaty. Harish said New Delhi had no intention of bringing bilateral issues into the discussion but was compelled to respond to Pakistan's attempt to misuse the forum.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday highlighted India's economic growth and poverty reduction at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) annual general meeting and convention, a day after Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi described the country as being in the grip of an “economic disaster”.Speaking at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, the PM said India was the world's fastest-growing major economy, with growth projected at around 7 per cent.“Today, India is the world's fastest-growing major economy, projected to grow at around 7%. In October, India's goods exports reached nearly $50 billion, our highest-ever monthly goods export,” Modi said.He added that agencies including Moody's Ratings, S&P Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank were revising their growth forecasts for India upwards.Citing a World Bank report, Modi said 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty in the past 12 to 13 years. He contrasted this with the Congress-era 'Garibi Hatao' slogan.“In the 1970s, when the 'Garibi Hatao' slogan was given, India's population was around 50 crore; poverty could have been eradicated then too, but FICCI is a witness that there was a flaw in policies and, unfortunately, a lack of the right intention,” he said.“When we worked with the right policies and the right intention, 50 crore poor people came out of poverty in just 12–13 years,” he added. PM's remarks came after Rahul Gandhi, speaking at Columbia University in New York, said India was “sitting on an economic disaster”, citing unemployment, a struggling manufacturing sector and problems in education.The Prime Minister also challenged businesses to stop treating Indian consumers as a market for lower-quality products.“Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted as an assured market where anything will sell. Even today, sellers tell customers 'this is export quality' to convince them it is good. What do you take our countrymen for? Do they not deserve good quality? This mindset must change; my countrymen deserve top quality,” he said.Referring to India's free trade agreements with major economies, Modi urged businesses to take advantage of expanded market access.“India has signed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with several major economies; doors have opened for you. Have you planned to seize this opportunity? If you do not take advantage of all my hard work, who will?” he said.Modi also cited tax reforms, including the reduction in the basic corporate tax rate from 30 per cent to 22 per cent and the exemption from income tax on earnings up to Rs 12 lakh.“Did you increase your employees' salaries or hire more staff?” he asked business leaders, while highlighting simplified tax returns and faster refunds.Recalling India's journey from the “License Quota Raj” to the “Fragile Five” period, Modi said young people, farmers, workers and industry leaders had helped transform the economy over the past 12 years.FICCI's centenary year marks 100 years since its establishment on April 7, 1927. The convention comes amid a wider political debate over economic growth, jobs and the distribution of its benefits.Modi also called on the pharmaceutical industry to reduce dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), bulk drugs and drug intermediates.“India is called the ‘pharmacy of the world,’ yet it imports billions of dollars' worth of APIs, bulk drugs, and drug intermediates every year,” he said.“There are hundreds of categories in which we currently depend on imports. Our pharmaceutical industry must understand which ingredients we can manufacture in India. In which areas can we invest in new technology and large production plants to become competitive with other countries?” he added.The Prime Minister also called for greater private investment in agriculture and urged businesses to develop products for overseas markets.“I would urge you to increase your industry’s investment in India’s agricultural sector. Set up reliable procurement systems with specific overseas markets in mind, and develop products for which there is demand there, so that Indian products can become our calling card around the world,” Modi said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi highlighted India's economic growth and poverty reduction at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) annual general meeting and convention. Article Title: Malaysia to not remain visa free for Indian visitors from Jan 1, 2027

NEW DELHI: Malaysia could, from Jan 1, 2027, withdraw its visa exemption policy for Indian visitors. The southeast Asian country had in Dec 2023 started this to boost tourism post Covid. While the immigration department of Malaysia announced last month “Indian nationals entering Malaysia from (Jan 1, 2027) onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival,” the Malaysian High Commission in Delhi told TOI Thursday the “visa-free (visa exemption facility) period tentatively ends on Dec 31, 2026.” Which means unless that facility is extended, going to Malaysia will require a visa from next year.While there was a surge in Indians visiting the country, the High Commission of India (HCI) in Kuala Lumpur had recently warned that there had been “a noticeable increase in Indian nationals arriving in Malaysia using the 30-day visa-free facility, to seek employment.” This, HCI had warned, “is a clear violation of immigration rules, as the visa-free entry facility which permits Indian passport holders to stay in Malaysia for up to 30 days is granted for tourism and social visits only.The immigration department of Malaysia (JIM) said in an announcement dated Nov 17, 2026: “…visa exemption facility for Indian nationals will no longer be available with effect from Jan 1, 2027. Accordingly, Indian nationals entering Malaysia from this date onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival. Visa applications may be submitted through the MyVISA portal starting Dec 1, 2026.” Other countries whose citizens require visa to enter Malaysia include Bangladesh, Bhutan, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal.The Malaysian High Commission in New Delhi told TOI Thursday: “Currently all Indian passport holders are allowed to enter and stay in Malaysia for up to 30 days only (for each entry) without any visa for tourism, business or social visits purposes. This Malaysia visa-free (visa exemption facility) period tentatively ends on Dec 31, 2026. Therefore, Indian Nationals entering Malaysia from Jan 1, 2027, onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa before arrival. ”Going visa free for Indians in Dec 2023 had led to Malaysia seeing a spike in visitor numbers from here. From just over 7.3 lakh Indian tourists in pre-Covid 2019, the number rose to 13.6 lakh in 2024; 15.6 lakh in 2025 and 7.4 lakh in Jan-June 2026 with a target of 21 lakh for this full calendar year.However, HCI, Kuala Lumpur had in a X post on Sept 22, 2026, warned against the misuse of tourist visas. “…Many Indian nationals are misled by unscrupulous agents with false job promises, leading to overstay, illegal status, exploitation, detention and legal action. This is a clear violation of immigration rules…. Genuine tourists must carry valid and verifiable documentation such as confirmed return ticket, hotel booking, online submission of the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) three days before the arrival date, and a passport with minimum 6-month validity, to avoid any immigration-related issues on arrival in Malaysia.Once again, Indian nationals are strictly advised not to travel to Malaysia for work / employment purpose without work permit or visa with reference (VDR),” the HCI post had added.The Malaysian immigration dept announcement of Nov 17 adds: “…all visa processing fees paid are strictly non-refundable, regardless of the application outcome, change of policy or any subsequent change to travel plans. JIM reserves the right to amend these entry requirements at any time in accordance with directives from govt of Malaysia.”
Article Summary: Malaysia could withdraw its visa exemption policy for Indian visitors from Jan 1, 2027. The decision comes after an increase in Indians misusing the visa-free entry for employment purposes. The southeast Asian country had in Dec 2023 started this to boost tourism post Covid.

Article Title: Health of states: Bihar per capita spend lowest, Sikkim's highest
Article Text:

Expenditure sheet

NEW DELHI: There are wide regional disparities on what govt spends on healthcare. Govt health expenditure per person in the four poorer northern states - Bihar, UP, MP and Jharkhand - averages around Rs 1,651, less than half the Rs 3,501 recorded in the northeastern states and nearly a fourth of the Rs 7,209 average for UTs, according to the National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates for 2023-24.At the national level, govt health expenditure stood at Rs 4.1 lakh crore in 2023-24, translating into Rs 2,959 per person. It accounted for 43.5% of total health expenditure and 1.43% of GDP.Southern states recorded a population-weighted average govt health spending of around Rs 2,960 per person, almost matching the national average of Rs 2,959. Kerala and Andhra Pradesh were above this level at Rs 3,396 and Rs 3,347, respectively, while Telangana spent Rs 3,125. Tamil Nadu's per capita spending stood at Rs 2,860 and Karnataka's at Rs 2,446, showing considerable variation even within the region."The differences and disparities in per capita govt health expenditure reflect differences in states' fiscal capacity, population size, historical investment in healthcare infrastructure and political priorities. Economically weaker, populous states face greater resource constraints and higher investment by govts, while northeastern states incur higher service delivery costs and higher per capita investment due to difficult terrain and dispersed populations," health policy specialist Dr Chandrakant Lahariya said."We need to remember some of the fixed costs such as capital investment, infrastructure cost remain relatively high even if people using those services are limited."The disparity is particularly stark in Bihar and UP, where govt health spending was Rs 1,126 and Rs 1,399 per person, respectively. In comparison, Sikkim spent Rs 16,026 per person, the highest among states, while Chandigarh led among UTs at Rs 24,187. The population-weighted average for the four poorer states worked out to Rs 1,651.The eight NE states show considerable variation. While Assam spends Rs 2,282 per person and Tripura Rs 3,360, spending is substantially higher in Sikkim (Rs 16,026), Mizoram (Rs 9,320), Arunachal (Rs 8,885) and Meghalaya (Rs 7,533). Manipur and Nagaland reported per capita spending of Rs 5,507 and Rs 4,585, respectively. The population-weighted regional average works out to around Rs 3,501.Among UTs, Puducherry spent Rs 11,165, Lakshadweep Rs 9,643, Andaman and Nicobar Islands at Rs 8,947 and Delhi at Rs 8,611. J&K reported Rs 3,339, while Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu recorded Rs 2,293. The population-weighted average across the seven UTs covered in the report was around Rs 7,209.The figures underline substantial geographical differences in public health financing, although per capita spending alone does not measure the quality, accessibility or outcomes of services.
Article Summary: Poorer northern states spend less than half of what Northeast spends per person. At the national level, govt health expenditure stood at Rs 4.1 lakh crore in 2023-24. Sikkim spent Rs 16,026 per person, the highest among states, while Chandigarh led among UTs at Rs 24,187.

New Delhi: Putting child rights at the heart of wellness, Unicef and the Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) have joined hands to encourage pediatricians to champion the cause through the ‘Child Rights Pledge Platform’ launched on Tuesday on the official IAP website.“The initiative aims to support pediatricians across India to become champions for children’s rights by strengthening their understanding of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) and promoting the integration of child rights principles into everyday interactions with children and their families,” IAP and Unicef said in a statement.The partnership aims to embed child rights into daily consultations by informing, educating, and engaging pediatricians on the Convention of the Rights of Child.Dr Neelam Mohan, president of IAP said, “For more than 50,000 pediatricians across India, this initiative is an opportunity to reaffirm our commitment not only to children’s health, but also to their rights and well-being holistically.”“We see children at every stage of their development and can recognise when their health, nutrition, development or well-being is compromised. We can identify and respond to abuse, neglect, exploitation, discrimination and other threats to children’s safety.We are trusted by families and communities, and our voices can influence attitudes, practices and behaviours,” she added.She asserted that given that pediatricians interact with children closely and can notice their challenges, it is crucial for them to be the voice of the children to safeguard their rights. “By taking the pledge, we commit to promoting, protecting and advancing the rights of every child through our daily interactions with children, families and communities,” she added.The platform allows the visitor to go through a simple guide on the rights of children enabling visitors to learn about not just rights focused on survival like life, health, nutrition, clean water and healthy environment but also on rights linked to development, protection, participation and non-discrimination, access and equity.A visitor can register with basic details like name and email to pledge support to secure the rights of children. Besides details on rights, the platform also showcases a short video by Unicef on the subject. The visitor can download their child rights champion certificate which can be displayed to express commitment and build awareness.The platform shows that by Wednesday evening, and a day since the launch, around 900 people had taken the pledge and been certified as child rights champions. They include health professionals, concerned citizens, parents and guardians, educators, teachers and IAP members and pediatricians.
Article Summary: Unicef and the Indian Academy of Pediatrics (IAP) have joined hands to encourage pediatricians to champion the cause. The ‘Child Rights Pledge Platform’ launched on Tuesday on the official IAP website. The initiative aims to support pediatricians across India to become champions for children’s rights.

NEW DELHI: Farmers on Wednesday sought access to the next generation of genetically modified crops and urged science-led decisions on farm technology during a media workshop organised by the National Farmers Empowerment Initiative in Ahmedabad.Farmers said India could not continue relying on two-decade-old cotton technology as new pests, erratic weather and rising cultivation costs demanded improved crop traits."Bt cotton made a difference to cotton cultivation in India. India released two genome-edited rice varieties in 2025."Farmers will adopt technologies that improve productivity and protect crops if they receive the right information and guidance. Agricultural policies must keep pace with science," said Mukesh Kantilal Patel, a farmer from Chanasma in Patan district.Bharat Char, chief science officer at Mahyco and head of the Alliance for Agri Innovation also called for continued field trials across agro-climatic zones and a predictable regulatory framework."Farmers deserve a choice of the best technologies available anywhere in the world. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.
