Article Title: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO: How can Indian investors buy shares in Claude's parent company
Article Text:
Anthropic shares: How can you invest

Here's how Indian investors can buy its shares

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

How much can Indian investors put into US stocks

NEW DELHI: Anthropic has just rewritten the IPO record books, raising $81.31 billion through its stock market offering and surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising haul. For investors who have watched the artificial intelligence race unfold from the sidelines, this could look like a chance to finally get a slice of the action.But for Indian investors hoping to own a piece of the company behind AI chatbot Claude, there is a catch: they will have to wait for its US market debut and buy shares at the prevailing market price, rather than the IPO offer price.Anthropic is scheduled to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026, under the ticker symbol “ANT”. With the IPO subscription window now closed, resident Indian investors who missed the offering cannot buy shares at the original offer price. Their entry point will instead depend on the stock's market price once trading begins, which could mean paying a premium.The offering has attracted strong interest from investors worldwide, with Anthropic expected to command a valuation of more than $1 trillion. This would place it among the world's most valuable publicly traded technology companies.The IPO comprises 980 million Class A common shares. Of these, Anthropic is offering 956.35 million shares, while certain existing shareholders are selling the remaining 23.65 million.The company has clarified that it will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by these existing shareholders.Missing the IPO subscription window does not necessarily mean missing out on the stock altogether. Once Anthropic begins trading in the US, Indian residents can purchase its shares through overseas brokerage accounts that provide access to Nasdaq-listed stocks.Investors can make these investments through the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) route. The process requires them to complete KYC formalities, submit the necessary tax documentation and transfer funds through an authorised banking channel.GIFT City-based investment platforms are another possible route, with some offering access to US equities. However, this depends on their product offerings and regulatory arrangements.Before choosing a platform, investors should check whether it will support trading in Anthropic shares from the listing date. Zerodha, Groww and HDFC Securities are among the stock brokerage platforms that offer access to overseas stocks.The RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme allows Indian residents to remit up to $250,000 per financial year for permitted purposes. The limit covers investments in foreign stocks and overseas-listed exchange-traded funds (ETFs), as well as expenses such as travel and education.Importantly, the entire $250,000 allowance can be used for investments in the US stock market, provided the investor does not need to use any part of it for other permitted overseas expenses during that financial year.For instance, if an investor does not plan to send money to children studying abroad or meet other eligible overseas expenses, the full annual remittance limit can be used for investments in US stocks.
Article Summary: Anthropic is scheduled to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026. Indian investors who missed the offering cannot buy shares at the original offer price. Their entry point will instead depend on the stock's market price once trading begins, which could mean paying a premium.

Article Title: SpiceJet is cancelling over half its scheduled flights daily, leaving passengers stranded as DGCA stops short of restricting bookings; cash-strapped airline races to raise Rs 5,500 crore
Article Text:
Despite SpiceJet’s failure to operate flights in line with its published timetable, DGCA has not, so far, barred the airline from accepting bookings.

SpiceJet cancels multiple flights

SpiceJet financial troubles

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In fresh trouble for the aviation sector, SpiceJet is reportedly cancelling more than half of its scheduled flights daily, leaving thousands of passengers facing disruptions as a severe cash shortage has grounded a large number of aircraft and put the budget carrier’s ability to continue operations at risk.Amid the financial strain, the airline’s board on Wednesday approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore.According to an ET report, airline executives have warned, however, that the carrier could be forced to shut down if fresh funds are not infused within a week.Despite SpiceJet’s failure to operate flights in line with its published timetable, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has not, so far, barred the airline from accepting bookings. The regulator’s decision not to impose restrictions has prompted questions about its reluctance to take action against the carrier.For the winter schedule, the DGCA had approved around 66 flights a day for SpiceJet.The airline, however, has been operating barely 15 daily flights while continuing to accept bookings across its entire schedule, the financial daily reported.Six aircraft taken on lease recently are still grounded because the airline has not paid the lessors, people familiar with the matter said.FLYONE, a Moldova-based airline that had leased three aircraft to SpiceJet, terminated its agreement on Monday over unpaid dues.On Tuesday, SpiceJet cancelled most of its departures from Mumbai, leaving thousands of passengers stranded.Biswajit Ghosh, an executive at FMCG major Nestle, was among those affected. Travelling to Darbhanga, he had paid Rs 10,600 for a one-way ticket but learnt that his flight had been cancelled only after arriving at the airport.“Passengers are bearing the brunt of cancellations despite booking tickets on an approved schedule,” he wrote on LinkedIn. “Should the survival of an airline come at the expense of passenger rights?”Several DGCA officials said the government is hesitant to instruct SpiceJet to stop accepting bookings for future flights, as such a move could push the airline towards shutting down its operations.“We have sent a show-cause notice to the airline as it has been unable to maintain its schedule,” a senior DGCA official was quoted as saying by ET. “The civil aviation ministry has to take a call on suspension of operations.”SpiceJet’s financial difficulties deepened after Yes Bank refused to provide a Rs 350 crore loan under the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS), citing the airline’s history of defaults, according to the people mentioned earlier.Chairman and managing director Ajay Singh met civil aviation secretary Samir Sinha last week and cautioned that the airline could struggle to keep operating without financial support from banks, they said.The latest developments have brought the DGCA’s regulatory oversight into focus. Before approving an airline’s flight schedule, the regulator assesses factors such as aircraft availability, the strength of its crew and its ability to operate the proposed services. Travel agents and industry executives have questioned why SpiceJet has been allowed to sell tickets for flights it cannot run according to its published timetable.
Article Summary: SpiceJet is reportedly cancelling more than half of its scheduled flights daily, leaving thousands of passengers facing disruptions. A severe cash shortage has grounded a large number of aircraft and put the budget carrier's ability to continue operations at risk. Despite SpiceJet’s failure to operate flights in line with its published timetable, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation has not, so far, barred the airline from accepting bookings.

Article Title: 'Must uphold open regionalism': Xi calls for free trade & stronger Asia-Pacific cooperation at APEC
Article Text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping speaks at the 2026 APEC CEO Summit held ahead of the APEC China 2026 summit in Shenzhen, southern China's Guangdong province.

Trump, Xi and Putin meeting amid geopolitical tensions

US-China trade tensions remain a challenge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for free and open trade, stronger regional cooperation and improved economic connectivity across the Asia-Pacific region, as leaders gathered for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen.Addressing the summit, Xi urged member economies to uphold open regionalism, strengthen economic cooperation and remove barriers that restrict trade and growth. His remarks come amid continuing trade tensions between the United States and China and growing geopolitical divisions over technology, security and global supply chains.Xi called for efforts to "unblock economic channels" and create more opportunities for growth across the Asia-Pacific region. He also advocated smart customs systems and better regional data governance to facilitate trade and improve economic connectivity.The Chinese president stressed the need to build an open and inclusive framework for regional cooperation rather than arrangements that exclude certain economies."We must uphold open regionalism, steadily promote economy, build open but not exclusive cooperation," Xi said, according to Reuters.His remarks also focused on the importance of free and open trade at a time when protectionist policies, tariffs and restrictions on critical technologies are reshaping global commerce.Xi's address comes as US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and the Chinese leader prepare for a high-profile trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit.The discussions are expected to cover nuclear arms control, the wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade disputes and competition over artificial intelligence.Trump has presented the meeting as an opportunity to negotiate with two of Washington's major geopolitical rivals and explore ways to address international conflicts.The trilateral engagement is particularly important following the expiration of the New START nuclear arms control treaty between Washington and Moscow in February 2026. Trump has expressed interest in negotiating a new agreement that would also include China.However, expectations of an immediate breakthrough remain limited, given differences in the countries' nuclear capabilities and strategic priorities.Despite diplomatic engagement between Trump and Xi, economic tensions between the world's two largest economies remain unresolved.The trade truce reached last year following reciprocal tariff increases is due to expire on January 10 next year. Washington has also accused Beijing of not fully honouring commitments to increase purchases of American agricultural products and ease restrictions on rare earth mineral exports.Competition over artificial intelligence and access to advanced semiconductors has added another dimension to the rivalry.Xi's call for open trade and regional economic cooperation therefore comes at a time when the Asia-Pacific region faces competing pressures from geopolitical rivalries, trade restrictions and disruptions to global supply chains.The APEC summit provides Beijing an opportunity to project itself as a supporter of regional economic integration while positioning China as a central player in shaping the future of Asia-Pacific cooperation.
Article Summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for free and open trade, stronger regional cooperation and improved economic connectivity across the Asia-Pacific region. His remarks come amid continuing trade tensions between the United States and China and growing geopolitical divisions over technology, security and global supply chains. Xi's address comes as US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and the Chinese leader prepare for a high-profile trilateral meeting.

Article Title: Gurgaon family cancels Jaipur destination wedding after groom’s father’s factory fire kills 14, resort refuses to refund Rs 16 lakh, consumer commission orders it to return Rs 16 lakh with interest an
Article Text:
(AI image) A family from Gurgaon canceled their planned destination wedding at The Rajasthali Resort & Spa in Jaipur.

GURGAON: A Gurgaon family’s decision to cancel a destination wedding at a Jaipur resort after a fire at the groom’s father’s factory killed 14 workers has resulted in a consumer commission directing the resort to refund Rs 16 lakh, with 9% annual interest, besides paying Rs 1.5 lakh as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 55,000 towards litigation expenses.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gurgaon, held The Rajasthali Resort & Spa, Jaipur, guilty of deficiency in service after it failed to refund the amount deposited by Gagan Bansal despite his requests to cancel the wedding functions following the tragedy.In its order, the commission directed the resort to refund the entire Rs 16 lakh along with interest at 9% per annum calculated from the dates of individual payments until realisation. It also directed the resort to pay the awarded amounts within 45 days of the order.According to the complaint, Bansal had booked the resort for his destination wedding after being attracted by offers of discounts and other facilities. He initially paid Rs 1 lakh in cash as booking money, followed by four RTGS transactions of Rs 4 lakh, Rs 5 lakh, Rs 4 lakh and Rs 2 lakh, taking the total payment to Rs 16 lakh.The dispute allegedly began when the resort sent him a draft contract after receiving the payments.Bansal told the commission that the draft contained increased rates and additional items in the paid list, contrary to the terms discussed during negotiations. Despite his objections, the resort allegedly insisted on the revised terms.The situation took a turn after a fire broke out at the groom’s father’s factory on May 28, 2024, engulfing 14 workers. The bride’s cousin was among those killed, while her uncle sustained injuries, the complaint stated.Bansal informed the resort about the tragedy on June 5, 2024, and sought cancellation of the wedding arrangements and a refund. He alleged that the resort threatened to forfeit the entire amount, questioning why the family had booked the property if it was not financially capable of proceeding with the wedding.The complaint further alleged that when Bansal’s father contacted the resort on July 11 to discuss cancellation and refund, a person identifying himself as its vice-president, Vichin Sehgal, misbehaved with him and threatened that he could face trouble from Jaipur Police if he visited the city.Advocate Sudesh K Kataria, appearing for Bansal, placed the complainant’s affidavit, bank statements, contract documents and newspaper reports relating to the factory fire before the commission.The resort, however, did not appear before the commission despite being served notice and was proceeded against ex parte on Aug 20, 2025. Consequently, there was no representation or evidence on its behalf to counter the allegations.The commission observed that there was nothing on record to disbelieve the complainant’s evidence. It also noted that the resort’s absence meant the evidence produced by Bansal remained unrebutted.Holding the resort guilty of deficiency in service, the commission allowed the complaint and ordered the refund with interest and compensation.The commission further warned that failure to comply with the order could lead to execution proceedings under Section 71(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and prosecution under Section 72, which provides for imprisonment of one month to three years, a fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh, or both.
Article Summary: A family from Gurgaon canceled their planned destination wedding at The Rajasthali Resort & Spa in Jaipur. A fire at the groom's father's factory killed 14 workers. A consumer commission directed the resort to refund Rs 16 lakh, with 9% annual interest, besides paying Rs 1.5 lakh as compensation.
